newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Murdoch's son continues rise up corporate ladder.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch's son continues rise up corporate ladder.

text.p: Lachlan Murdoch, the elder son of Rupert Murdoch, continued his rapid rise through the ranks of his father's global media empire News Corp. on Monday when he was appointed managing director of the group's Australian operation.
Lachlan joined News Ltd, the Australian subsidiary of News Corp, as general manager of the company's Queensland Newspapers business in 1994.
He will now be responsible for managing all News Ltd. operations, which mainly comprise newspapers, investments in magazines and television, and a 50 percent stake in airline Ansett Australia.
The appointment will not affect the role of News Ltd. Chairman and Chief Executive Ken Cowley, a long time confidant of Rupert Murdoch and a member of the News Corp. board.
"I will remain intimately in the business as executive Chairman of News Ltd. as well as continuing to hold a range of directorships," Cowley said in a statement.

"My primary function will be to shape the strategic direction of the group's businesses at a time when traditional media is confronting its greatest challenges from technological change and increased competition," Cowley said.
"Lachlan will concentrate on managing the News group operations and will report to me," he said.
Lachlan Murdoch, 25, is also a director of Murdoch's joint venture in China with The People's Daily and deputy chairman of Hong Kong-based satellite broadcaster STAR TV.
He does not have a seat on the board but is on the group's executive committee which was formed in late 1995.
Lachlan is one of two Murdoch children employed in the News Corp. business. Murdoch's daughter Elizabeth was appointed general manager, broadcasting, of British Sky Broadcasting in February.
Murdoch's other son, James, and daughter, Prudence, are not involved in the A$18.9 billion ($14.9 billion) family business, but his wife Anna is on the board.
The latest appointment is likely to stir some speculation about who will eventually succeed Rupert Murdoch as head of the News Corp. but analysts said Lachlan still had a way to go to prove himself.
"I wouldn't read too much into it," said Nola Hodgson, media analyst at SBC James Capel.
"Rupert Murdoch is likely to be around for some time yet."
Murdoch, 65, inherited control of the News group from his late father Sir Keith Murdoch in 1952.
The Murdoch family owns about 30 percent of News Corp.
